files_changed.summary: RunContext (detached-context helper, DefaultRunBudget=15min), Hub (per-RunID topic, bounded ring-buffer replay, bounded per-subscriber channel), Publish (non-blocking, drops slow subscribers), Subscribe (replay + live channel + idempotent unsubscribe), Close (tears down a run's topic, closes all subscriber channels).

10 tests: basic delivery, replay-after-seq, ring-buffer eviction, slow-subscriber drop, unsubscribe (incl. double-unsubscribe), Close (incl. double-close), a concurrent Publish/Subscribe smoke test, and 3 RunContext tests (survives parent cancel, own timeout, own explicit cancel).

decisions: No goroutines spawned by hub.go (confirmed by design, not just by luck): Publish/Subscribe/Close are synchronous and mutex-protected; context.WithTimeout/WithoutCancel are stdlib composition. This keeps the file entirely outside §7.1's 'no bare go outside shared/concurrency' rule.

Used plain sync.Mutex per topic instead of the doc's literal sync.RWMutex wording — every operation here mutates shared state, so RWMutex would add complexity with no read-only fast path to justify it. Documented as a deliberate non-functional deviation, not a scope gap (see analyze.json risks).

No wiring into Service.StartRun or httpapi (confirmed twice with user, after checking 00-thinkboard-abstract-plan.md for any conflicting signal): this task delivers the Hub mechanism itself ('the streaming contract'), not the async orchestrator/SSE-handler wiring that consumes it.
Event.Payload is 'any' (opaque) — Hub is content-agnostic; real event shapes arrive once orchestrator.go actually publishes to a Hub.
